C. V. Raman was an Indian physicist, born in 1888 in Tiruchirappalli, who discovered the Raman effect in Calcutta in 1928 and won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930, the first Asian to win a Nobel in science.

He began as a government accountant in Calcutta and did research in his spare hours at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science. In 1917 he became a professor at the University of Calcutta.

On 28 February 1928, with his student K. S. Krishnan, he showed that when light passes through a liquid, a tiny part of it comes out at a changed colour, shifted by the vibrations of the molecules. This Raman scattering is now used everywhere to identify substances. India marks the day as National Science Day.

He later led the Indian Institute of Science in Bangalore and founded his own research institute there. He was one of the scientists, with Ramanujan and S. N. Bose, who showed that world class work could be done in colonial India. His nephew Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar also won a Nobel.
sum: C. V. Raman was an Indian physicist, born in 1888 in Tiruchirappalli, who discovered the Raman effect in Calcutta in 1928 and won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930, the first Asian to win a Nobel in science.
